title: Study Advice
summary: We listened to two teachers talking about a student who has problems with speaking. We learned the second conditional for imaginary situations and used 'If I were you, I would...' to give advice. Then we shared study tips for learners of English.

grammar.title: Second conditional
grammar.explain: We use the second conditional to talk about imaginary or unlikely situations in the present or future, and their results. The if-clause uses the past simple, but the meaning is not past.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم الجملة الشرطية الثانية للحديث عن مواقف خيالية أو غير مرجّحة في الحاضر أو المستقبل ونتائجها. نضع الفعل بعد if في الماضي البسيط، لكن المعنى ليس في الماضي، ونستخدم would + الفعل المجرّد في الجملة الرئيسية.
form: If + past simple, would + base verb: If I had more time, I would do it myself.
would + base verb + if + past simple (no comma): I would do it myself if I had more time.
could / might + base verb can replace would: If you had a good job, you could save some money.
Question: What would you do if you found a wallet in the street?

examples.en: If I had this problem, I would try to identify the reason first.
examples.note: Maggie imagines she has John's problem.

examples.en: If the weather was nicer, we would have a picnic.
examples.note: The weather is not nice now, so we are not having a picnic.

examples.en: What would you do if you had a time machine?
If you had a good job, you could save some money.
You would make more friends if you joined a sports club.
examples.note: When the if-clause comes second, there is no comma.

mistakes.wrong: If I would have more time, I would help you.
mistakes.right: If I had more time, I would help you.
mistakes.why: Do not use 'would' in the if-clause. Use the past simple.

mistakes.wrong: If I had a lot of money, I will buy a big house.
mistakes.right: If I had a lot of money, I would buy a big house.

mistakes.wrong: If you have the ability not to work, you will not work.
mistakes.right: If you had the ability not to work, you would not work.
mistakes.why: This is imaginary, so use the second conditional: had ... would.

mistakes.wrong: She would go by plane, if it was cheaper.
mistakes.right: She would go by plane if it was cheaper.
mistakes.why: We only use a comma when the if-clause comes first.

quiz.q: If the weather ___ nicer, we would have a picnic.
She ___ by plane if it was cheaper.
quiz.why: The main clause uses would + base verb.

quiz.q: What would you do if you ___ a wallet in the street?
quiz.why: The if-clause uses the past simple: found.

quiz.q: If you had a good job, you ___ save some money.
quiz.why: 'could' is the past of 'can' and means 'would be able to'.

quiz.q: She would look much better if she ___ her hairstyle.
'If I lived to be 120, I would travel more.' This sentence is about...
quiz.why: The second conditional talks about imaginary situations.

grammar.title: Giving advice: If I were you, I would...
grammar.explain: To give advice, we imagine that we are the other person. We say 'If I were you, I would (not) ...'. In this phrase we use 'were', not 'was'.
grammar.explain_ar: لإعطاء نصيحة نتخيّل أننا مكان الشخص الآخر، فنقول: If I were you, I would… أو I wouldn't… للنصيحة بعدم فعل شيء. في هذه العبارة نستخدم were وليس was.
form: If I were you, I would / I'd + base verb
If I were you, I wouldn't + base verb
I would / I'd + base verb + if I were you.

examples.en: If I were you, I would teach him to paraphrase.
examples.note: Maggie's advice to John about his student.

examples.en: If I were you, I wouldn't go out with him.
I'd buy the blue suit if I were you.
A: I don't have any money. B: If I were you, I would borrow some from a friend.

mistakes.wrong: If I was you, I would call her.
mistakes.right: If I were you, I would call her.
mistakes.why: In the advice phrase we say 'If I were you'.

mistakes.wrong: If I were you, I will call her.
mistakes.right: If I were you, I would call her.

mistakes.wrong: If I were you, I would to call her.
mistakes.right: If I were you, I would call her.

quiz.q: If I ___ you, I would join a sports club.
quiz.why: The fixed phrase is 'If I were you'.

quiz.q: If I were you, I ___ go out with him.
quiz.why: Advice not to do something: wouldn't + base verb.

quiz.q: I'm bored. — If I were you, I ___ a new hobby.

options: If I was you, I will rest.
If I were you, I would rest.
If I were you, I rest.
quiz.why: If I were you + would + base verb.

quiz.q: I'm stressed out. — ___ take a short break if I were you.

If I were you, I wouldn't ...
phrases.use: Advising someone not to do something

phrases.use: Praising someone in front of a group
